title: ‘This Is Not a Drill’: Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Are Setting the Internet on Fire
gist: The PHP Foundation shipped emergency patches on October 21 for two critical (CVSS 9.2) flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, affecting all PHP installs back to version 5 and enabling unauthenticated remote code execution or memory reads. Cloudflare saw early attacks, some European government sites went offline, and experts say AI shortens time-to-exploit to minutes.

insights.claim: The PHP Foundation disclosed two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each rated 9.2 of 10 on CVSS, affecting all PHP installations serving web requests going back to PHP 5 (July 2004).
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Scale of exposure spans WordPress, Drupal and Magento stacks; patch urgency drives security-vendor demand.
insights.locator: The PHP Foundation detailed the two critical vulnerabilities

insights.claim: Only PHP 8.2 and newer receive official patches, so legacy PHP deployments forgotten in old infrastructure remain exposed unless third-party vendors supply fixes.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Long tail of unmaintained PHP is the main residual risk; audit legacy estates.

insights.claim: Wiz says the flaws let unauthenticated attackers execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory that may hold passwords, tokens, API keys and certificates.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Credential leakage extends the blast radius beyond the compromised server.
insights.quote: The vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers or read sensitive process memory

insights.claim: The PHP Foundation stated that there are no complete mitigations and that updating is the only safe choice.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: No workaround means patch speed determines exposure.
insights.quote: There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice

insights.claim: Cloudflare reported early attacks emerging before the PHP Foundation published details, and Sansec expected mass attacks within 15 minutes of the release.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Window between disclosure and exploitation is now minutes, favoring automated defenses.
insights.quote: We expect mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release

insights.claim: Lukasz Olejnik warns the worst case is wormable malware affecting large chunks of the internet and says AI makes exploiting such vulnerabilities a matter of about a minute.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: AI compresses exploit development, raising tail risk of internet-scale incidents.
insights.quote: AI makes exploiting such vulnerabilities of immediate importance. Like, indeed, a minute or so.

insights.claim: Davi Ottenheimer describes the bug as sitting in a file upload interface like a front door with no lock, exploitable with one crafted upload to any server without knowing the site or software.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Attack requires no targeting, so scanning-based mass exploitation is cheap.
insights.locator: “Most of the web runs on PHP

insights.claim: Some organizations took sites offline before patches arrived, including multiple Finnish government sites, French government websites and the Port of Rotterdam.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Precautionary outages show real operational cost of the disclosure.
insights.locator: Ahead of the updated versions of PHP becoming available

insights.claim: Google-owned Wiz says its researchers found the vulnerabilities partly using AI tools, while OpenAI and security firm Calif say they independently discovered them and worked together.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Three parties finding the same bugs with AI suggests AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is mainstream.
insights.locator: Security company Wiz, which is owned by Google

insights.claim: The UK NCSC told organizations to prepare for immediate updating and to consider taking systems offline if remediation is not feasible, while EU-CERT and Australia's cyber agency also issued warnings.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
insights.so_what: Official guidance accelerates enterprise patch and downtime decisions.
insights.locator: Similarly, the UK’s National Cyber Security Center

insights.claim: The FBI's Brett Leatherman urged victims to isolate compromised systems, preserve web server and PHP logs, and report to their local FBI field office.
insights.speaker: Matt Burgess
